title: Navigate and inspect files
summary: Navigate and inspect files in a developer shell.
syntax:
cd [directory]
pwd
ls [-lah] [path]
rules: Quote paths containing spaces; cd changes the current shell directory.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Find files by name
summary: Find files by name in a developer shell.
syntax: find [path] -type f -name "pattern"
rules: Quote glob patterns so find receives them unchanged.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Search source text
summary: Search source text in a developer shell.
syntax:
rg [-n] [--glob pattern] pattern [path]
grep -n pattern file
rules: rg is an optional tool; quote regexes and globs.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Filter and count a stream
summary: Filter and count a stream in a developer shell.
syntax:
command | command
sort [file]
uniq [-c]
wc [-l]
head -n count
tail -n count
rules: A pipe sends standard output to the next command; uniq only combines adjacent duplicates.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Redirect output and errors
summary: Redirect output and errors in a developer shell.
syntax:
command > file
command >> file
command 2>&1 | tee file
rules: The > operator overwrites a file; >> appends. Redirection order matters.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Set an environment variable
summary: Set an environment variable in a developer shell.
syntax:
export NAME=value
NAME=value command
env
rules: Assignment before a command applies to that command only in POSIX shells.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Quote paths and expansions
summary: Quote paths and expansions in a developer shell.
syntax:
"$variable"
'literal text'
$(command)
printf "%s\n" "$value"
rules: Double quotes preserve spaces while allowing expansion; single quotes suppress expansion.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Run commands on success
summary: Run commands on success in a developer shell.
syntax:
command && next
command || fallback
test -f path
if command; then commands; fi
rules: && runs after success; || runs after a nonzero exit status.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Process matching files
summary: Process matching files in a developer shell.
syntax:
for name in words; do commands; done
while command; do commands; done
rules: Quote expanded file names. Unmatched globs may remain literal in POSIX shells.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Review local Git changes
summary: Review local Git changes in a developer shell.
syntax:
git status [--short]
git diff [--staged] [-- path]
rules: git diff shows unstaged changes; --staged shows the index.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Create a feature branch
summary: Create a feature branch in a developer shell.
syntax:
git switch [-c] branch
git branch [--show-current]
rules: -c creates a branch from the current commit; an existing branch needs no -c.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Inspect recent commits
summary: Inspect recent commits in a developer shell.
syntax:
git log [--oneline] [-n count]
git show [commit]
rules: HEAD identifies the current commit.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Check Rust code
summary: Check Rust code in a developer shell.
syntax:
cargo check [--all-targets]
cargo build [--release]
rules: Run inside a Cargo project; check skips final code generation.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Run Rust tests
summary: Run Rust tests in a developer shell.
syntax: cargo test [filter] [--workspace] [-- test-options]
rules: Arguments after -- go to the test harness.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Run a Rust program
summary: Run a Rust program in a developer shell.
syntax: cargo run [--bin name] [--release] -- [arguments]
rules: Arguments after -- go to the executable.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Format and lint Rust
summary: Format and lint Rust in a developer shell.
syntax:
cargo fmt [--all] -- [--check]
cargo clippy [--all-targets] -- [-D warnings]
rules: rustfmt and clippy components must be installed; --check avoids modifying files.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Run Go tests
summary: Run Go tests in a developer shell.
syntax: go test [packages] [-run regexp] [-race]
rules: ./... includes packages below the current module; race testing needs a supported platform/toolchain.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Build or run Go
summary: Build or run Go in a developer shell.
syntax:
go build [packages]
go run package [arguments]
rules: Run from a Go module; go run compiles and executes a main package.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

references.title: Go command: Compile packages and dependencies

title: Format and vet Go
summary: Format and vet Go in a developer shell.
syntax:
gofmt [-l | -w] [path]
go fmt [packages]
go vet [packages]
rules: gofmt -l lists files; -w and go fmt rewrite them.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Maintain Go dependencies
summary: Maintain Go dependencies in a developer shell.
syntax:
go mod tidy
go mod download
go get module@version
rules: tidy updates go.mod and go.sum; dependency operations can access the network.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Reproducible dependency installs
summary: Reproducible dependency installs from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.
syntax:
pnpm install [--frozen-lockfile] [--prod]
npm ci [--omit=dev]
npm install
rules: Commit the lockfile for the chosen package manager. Frozen installs reject manifest mismatches.
npm ci requires package-lock.json and replaces node_modules; installs may execute package lifecycle scripts.
Reference: https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-ci/

title: Run scripts and pass arguments
summary: Run scripts and pass arguments from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.
syntax:
pnpm run <script> [arguments]
npm run <script> -- [arguments]
pnpm test
npm test
rules: Scripts come from package.json and run with local node_modules/.bin on PATH.
Put npm script arguments after --; pnpm forwards arguments following the script name.
Reference: https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-run-script/

title: Type-check a TypeScript project
summary: Type-check a TypeScript project from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.
syntax: tsc --project <directory-or-config> [--noEmit]
rules: Use the locally installed compiler. --noEmit checks without producing JavaScript.
Passing input files directly bypasses tsconfig.json; use --project to select a configured project.
Reference: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/compiler-options.html

title: Select Node with nvm
summary: Select Node with nvm from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.
syntax:
nvm install [version]
nvm use [version]
nvm current
node --version
rules: Load nvm in the shell first. Without a version, install/use reads .nvmrc.
Use the repository runtime and package-manager version; changing Node may change available global tools.
Reference: https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm#usage

title: Inspect an HTTP response
summary: Inspect an HTTP response in a developer shell.
syntax: curl [--fail] [--show-error] [--include] URL
rules: --fail returns a failure status for HTTP errors; --include prints response headers.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: Inspect running processes
summary: Inspect running processes in a developer shell.
syntax:
ps [-ef]
pgrep [-af] pattern
rules: Options vary across platforms; these examples target Linux developer shells.
Examples target Bash/Zsh and POSIX-style shell syntax; PowerShell and fish may differ.

title: AWS CLI command structure and help
summary: Select a service and operation, then supply parameters and global options.
syntax:
aws --version
aws help
aws SERVICE help
aws SERVICE OPERATION help
aws [--profile NAME] [--region REGION] SERVICE OPERATION [PARAMETERS] [--no-cli-pager]
rules: Use service-specific help to discover required parameters; high-level s3 commands differ from s3api operations.
CLI options override profile/environment settings for that call. The extension displays commands and never executes them.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-usage-commandstructure.html

references.title: AWS CLI v2: AWS CLI command structure and help

title: AWS profiles, SSO and caller identity
summary: Configure an IAM Identity Center profile, refresh its session, and confirm the account and role before using services.
syntax:
aws configure sso [--profile NAME]
aws sso login --profile NAME
aws configure list-profiles
aws configure list [--profile NAME]
aws sts get-caller-identity [--profile NAME]
aws sts assume-role --role-arn ARN --role-session-name NAME
rules: SSO requires an existing IAM Identity Center setup and browser authentication; configure sso saves local profile settings.
Use --profile/--region explicitly when switching accounts. Environment credentials can affect credential resolution.
assume-role returns temporary credentials, not a persistent login; treat credentials and debug output as secrets.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-sso.html

references.title: AWS CLI v2: AWS profiles, SSO and caller identity

title: AWS filtering, output and pagination
summary: Combine service-side filters with a client-side JMESPath projection and choose output suitable for humans or scripts.
syntax:
aws SERVICE OPERATION --query 'JMESPATH' --output json|text|table --no-cli-pager
aws SERVICE LIST_OPERATION [--page-size N] [--max-items N] [--starting-token TOKEN]
rules: Service filters reduce data returned by AWS; --query filters the received response locally.
--page-size changes API request size, not total results; --max-items caps CLI results and can return NextToken for --starting-token.
Auto-pagination is on by default. --no-paginate fetches only one page; --no-cli-pager only disables the display pager.
With --output text, queries can run once per page. Prefer JSON when sorting or aggregating the full response.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-usage-filter.html

references.title: AWS CLI v2: AWS filtering, output and pagination

title: S3 list, copy and presigned URLs
summary: Use the high-level S3 commands for object listings and transfers between local files and S3 URIs.
syntax:
aws s3 ls [s3://BUCKET/PREFIX] [--recursive]
aws s3 cp SOURCE DESTINATION [--recursive] [--dryrun]
aws s3 presign s3://BUCKET/KEY [--expires-in SECONDS]
rules: Quote S3 URIs and local paths containing spaces. cp uploads, downloads or copies depending on its arguments.
cp can overwrite the destination. Use --dryrun for a transfer preview.
A presigned URL grants access to its holder until expiry or credential expiry; do not publish it.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3/index.html

references.title: AWS CLI v2: S3 list, copy and presigned URLs

title: S3 directory synchronization
summary: Synchronize new and changed files between a local directory and an S3 prefix.
syntax:
aws s3 sync SOURCE DESTINATION [--dryrun] [--delete]
aws s3 sync SOURCE DESTINATION --exclude 'PATTERN' --include 'PATTERN'
rules: Always verify source/destination direction; remove --dryrun to perform writes.
--delete removes destination objects absent from the source and is not needed for an additive backup.
Include/exclude rules are processed in order; later matching rules win. Uploads follow symlinks by default.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3/sync.html

references.title: AWS CLI v2: S3 directory synchronization

title: S3 API metadata and object listings
summary: Use low-level S3 operations when structured JSON, object metadata or API pagination is needed.
syntax:
aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket BUCKET [--prefix PREFIX]
aws s3api head-object --bucket BUCKET --key KEY
aws s3api get-bucket-location --bucket BUCKET
rules: Use --bucket and --key rather than an s3:// URI for these operations.
head-object returns metadata without downloading the body. Missing permissions may look like missing objects.
The CLI handles list pagination by default; CLI --starting-token and service --continuation-token are different interfaces.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/s3api/index.html

references.title: AWS CLI v2: S3 API metadata and object listings

title: EC2 inventory, filters and waiters
summary: Inspect instance state and network information with describe operations and wait for a known resource state.
syntax:
aws ec2 describe-instances [--instance-ids ID ...] [--filters Name=NAME,Values=VALUE]
aws ec2 describe-security-groups [--group-ids ID ...]
aws ec2 wait instance-running --instance-ids ID
rules: Describe operations are read-only. Multiple filters combine with AND; values in a single filter combine with OR.
A waiter polls until success or timeout; it does not start an instance. Check its exit status.
Starting/stopping instances changes resources and can affect cost or availability; verify account, region and IDs.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/ec2/describe-instances.html

references.title: AWS CLI v2: EC2 inventory, filters and waiters

title: IAM roles and attached policies
summary: Inspect role trust policies and attached managed permissions without modifying IAM.
syntax:
aws iam list-roles
aws iam get-role --role-name NAME
aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name NAME
rules: A role trust policy determines who may assume it; attached permissions determine what the role may do.
list-attached-role-policies does not include inline policies or all effective permissions; boundaries and organization policies can also restrict access.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/iam/get-role.html

references.title: AWS CLI v2: IAM roles and attached policies

title: CloudWatch Logs tailing and filtering
summary: Follow a log group or retrieve events using a CloudWatch Logs filter pattern.
syntax:
aws logs describe-log-groups [--log-group-name-prefix PREFIX]
aws logs tail GROUP [--since 10m] [--follow] [--format short]
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name GROUP [--filter-pattern PATTERN]
rules: tail --follow keeps polling until interrupted; logs can contain personal data and secrets.
filter-log-events uses CloudWatch filter syntax, not JMESPath or a shell regular expression.
Select the region containing the log group; log retrieval may incur charges.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/logs/tail.html

references.title: AWS CLI v2: CloudWatch Logs tailing and filtering

title: Lambda inspection, invocation and code updates
summary: Inspect functions, invoke a test event or upload a deployment ZIP.
syntax:
aws lambda list-functions
aws lambda get-function-configuration --function-name NAME
aws lambda invoke --function-name NAME --payload fileb://EVENT.json RESPONSE.json
aws lambda update-function-code --function-name NAME --zip-file fileb://FUNCTION.zip
rules: fileb:// reads raw bytes regardless of --cli-binary-format; file:// JSON blobs otherwise follow the CLI binary format setting.
A synchronous invoke writes a response file and may report FunctionError even when the HTTP request succeeded.
Invocations can cause application side effects and charges. Code updates change the deployed function.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/lambda/invoke.html

references.title: AWS CLI v2: Lambda inspection, invocation and code updates

title: CloudFormation stack inspection and deployment previews
summary: Inspect stack outputs/events and prepare a change set for review before deployment.
syntax:
aws cloudformation describe-stacks --stack-name NAME
aws cloudformation describe-stack-events --stack-name NAME
aws cloudformation deploy --template-file FILE --stack-name NAME [--parameter-overrides KEY=VALUE ...] [--no-execute-changeset]
aws cloudformation describe-change-set --change-set-name NAME --stack-name NAME
rules: deploy normally creates and executes a change set; --no-execute-changeset creates it without applying the infrastructure changes.
Templates creating IAM resources may require CAPABILITY_IAM or CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM; acknowledge only after reviewing the template.
Review replacements, deletions and costs. Never assume a deployment is harmless because its change set is small.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/cloudformation/deploy.html

references.title: AWS CLI v2: CloudFormation stack inspection and deployment previews

title: DynamoDB typed keys and queries
summary: Read a typed primary key or query items sharing a partition-key value.
syntax:
aws dynamodb get-item --table-name TABLE --key '{"PK":{"S":"VALUE"}}'
aws dynamodb query --table-name TABLE --key-condition-expression '#pk = :pk' --expression-attribute-names '{"#pk":"PK"}' --expression-attribute-values '{":pk":{"S":"VALUE"}}'
rules: The low-level CLI uses AttributeValue types such as S, N and BOOL. N values are strings containing numbers.
Supply the complete primary key for get-item, including the sort key if the table has one.
query requires partition-key equality, optionally with a sort-key condition. A scan reads the table broadly and can be expensive.
Filter expressions run after reads; they do not reduce consumed read capacity.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/dynamodb/query.html

references.title: AWS CLI v2: DynamoDB typed keys and queries

title: SSM Parameter Store and managed sessions
summary: Read configuration parameters or open a Session Manager connection to a managed node.
syntax:
aws ssm get-parameter --name NAME [--with-decryption]
aws ssm get-parameters-by-path --path PATH [--recursive] [--with-decryption]
aws ssm start-session --target NODE_ID
rules: --with-decryption decrypts SecureString values when permissions allow; never print decrypted secrets into shared logs.
Recursive path permissions can expose descendants; request only the required path.
start-session requires the Session Manager plugin, a managed node and appropriate IAM/network setup.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/ssm/get-parameter.html

references.title: AWS CLI v2: SSM Parameter Store and managed sessions

title: Secrets Manager metadata and values
summary: Inspect secret metadata separately from retrieving the secret payload.
syntax:
aws secretsmanager describe-secret --secret-id NAME_OR_ARN
aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id NAME_OR_ARN [--version-stage AWSCURRENT]
rules: describe-secret returns metadata, not the secret value.
get-secret-value returns SecretString or SecretBinary; fetching/decrypting requires the relevant permissions.
Never copy plaintext secrets into tickets, terminal captures or shared files; retrieving secrets can incur API charges.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/secretsmanager/get-secret-value.html

title: ECR registry authentication and image inspection
summary: Authenticate Docker to a private ECR registry and inspect repository images.
syntax:
aws ecr get-login-password --region REGION | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin ACCOUNT.dkr.ecr.REGION.amazonaws.com
aws ecr describe-images --repository-name NAME
aws ecr list-images --repository-name NAME
rules: The ECR region must match the registry endpoint; authorization tokens last 12 hours.
Pipe the password directly to docker login --password-stdin; Docker saves registry authentication locally.
Login does not push an image. Image operations need repository permissions and the correct account/region.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/ecr/get-login-password.html

references.title: AWS CLI v2: ECR registry authentication and image inspection

title: ECS services, tasks and deployment status
summary: Discover ECS services and tasks and inspect deployment health.
syntax:
aws ecs list-services --cluster CLUSTER
aws ecs describe-services --cluster CLUSTER --services SERVICE ...
aws ecs list-tasks --cluster CLUSTER [--service-name SERVICE]
aws ecs describe-tasks --cluster CLUSTER --tasks TASK_ARN ...
aws ecs wait services-stable --cluster CLUSTER --services SERVICE
rules: Specify the cluster and region explicitly; describe operations can return a failures array as well as resource data.
services-stable polls scheduler state; it does not verify application-level health.
update-service --force-new-deployment restarts deployment and can affect availability; inspection does not require it.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/ecs/describe-services.html

title: EKS cluster inspection and kubeconfig
summary: Inspect EKS clusters and generate kubectl configuration for a selected cluster.
syntax:
aws eks list-clusters
aws eks describe-cluster --name NAME
aws eks update-kubeconfig --name NAME [--alias ALIAS] [--kubeconfig PATH] [--dry-run]
rules: update-kubeconfig normally writes/merges local kubeconfig and changes its current context; --dry-run prints the merged configuration instead.
kubectl needs separate installation plus cluster authorization and network access. Generating configuration does not grant permissions.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/eks/update-kubeconfig.html

references.title: AWS CLI v2: EKS cluster inspection and kubeconfig

title: CloudWatch metrics and alarms
summary: Discover metric dimensions, read time-series statistics and inspect alarm state.
syntax:
aws cloudwatch list-metrics --namespace NAMESPACE [--metric-name NAME]
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace NAMESPACE --metric-name NAME --start-time ISO8601 --end-time ISO8601 --period SECONDS --statistics Average [--dimensions Name=NAME,Value=VALUE]
aws cloudwatch describe-alarms [--state-value ALARM|OK|INSUFFICIENT_DATA]
rules: Metric namespace, name and complete dimension set identify the series; timestamps use UTC/ISO 8601.
Period must satisfy retention/resolution limits; returned datapoints are not guaranteed to be time ordered.
CloudWatch metrics and CloudWatch Logs use separate CLI services: cloudwatch and logs.
AWS CLI v2; Bash/Zsh quoting. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/cloudwatch/get-metric-statistics.html

references.title: AWS CLI v2: CloudWatch metrics and alarms

node [options] <entry.js> [arguments]
node --eval <code>
node --print <expression>
node --check <file>

--check parses without execution. Application arguments follow the entry file.

summary: Restart Node when files change from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.

rules: Watch mode restarts the entry process after changes to watched files.

summary: Debug Node and load environment files from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.

title: Add and remove packages
summary: Add and remove packages from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.
syntax:
pnpm add [-D] <package>
pnpm remove <package>
npm install [--save-dev] <package>
npm uninstall <package>
rules: Runtime dependencies go in dependencies; build/test tools usually go in devDependencies.
These commands change manifests/lockfiles and can download or execute package code. Review changes.
Reference: https://pnpm.io/cli/add

title: Review and update dependencies
summary: Review and update dependencies from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.
syntax:
pnpm outdated
pnpm update [package] [--latest]
npm outdated
npm update [package]
rules: outdated reports available versions; update normally respects manifest ranges.
pnpm update --latest can cross major versions and changes ranges; review migration notes and rerun checks.
Reference: https://pnpm.io/cli/update

title: Explain the dependency tree
summary: Explain the dependency tree from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.
syntax:
pnpm list [--depth <n>]
pnpm why <package>
npm ls [--depth=<n>]
npm explain <package>
rules: list/ls show installed dependencies; why/explain trace why a package is present.
Missing or invalid dependencies can produce nonzero statuses; transitive dependencies are not direct declarations.
Reference: https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-explain/

title: Inspect dependency advisories
summary: Inspect dependency advisories from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.
syntax:
pnpm audit [--prod]
npm audit [--omit=dev] [--audit-level=high]
rules: Audits contact the registry and can send dependency metadata. Findings require human assessment.
Avoid automatic force fixes: major updates can break the application. No findings does not establish safety.
Reference: https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-audit/

title: Target packages in a workspace
summary: Target packages in a workspace from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.
syntax:
pnpm --filter <selector> run <script>
pnpm -r run <script>
npm run <script> --workspace=<name>
npm run <script> --workspaces
rules: pnpm workspaces require pnpm-workspace.yaml; npm uses package.json workspaces.
Quote selectors containing shell metacharacters. Scripts must exist in selected packages.
Reference: https://pnpm.io/filtering

summary: Execute local and temporary CLI tools from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.

pnpm exec <binary> [arguments]
npx --no-install <binary> [arguments]
pnpm dlx <package>@<version> [arguments]
npm exec -- <binary> [arguments]
rules: exec uses project binaries; npx --no-install avoids fetching a missing executable.
dlx and unqualified npx/npm exec may fetch and run package code; pin and trust the package before use.

title: Build TypeScript project references
summary: Build TypeScript project references from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.
syntax:
tsc --build [projects...] [--watch]
tsc --build [projects...] --clean
rules: Build mode orders referenced projects and rebuilds out-of-date outputs. Referenced projects need composite configuration.
--clean deletes generated outputs; noEmit type checking and emitting referenced-project builds serve different purposes.
Reference: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/project-references.html

title: Inspect TypeScript config and resolution
summary: Inspect TypeScript config and resolution from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.
syntax:
tsc --init
tsc --project <config> --showConfig
tsc --project <config> --traceResolution --noEmit
rules: --showConfig prints the effective configuration including inherited settings.
--traceResolution diagnoses import lookup and can produce large path-containing logs; --init creates a config in a new project.
Reference: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/compiler-options.html

title: Lint with ESLint
summary: Lint with ESLint from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.
syntax:
eslint <files...> [--max-warnings <n>]
eslint <files...> --fix
eslint --print-config <file>
rules: Requires local ESLint and a compatible eslint.config.js; TypeScript needs a configured TypeScript parser/plugin.
--fix edits files. --max-warnings 0 makes warnings fail CI; inspect effective config with --print-config.
Reference: https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/command-line-interface

title: Check and apply Prettier formatting
summary: Check and apply Prettier formatting from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.
syntax:
prettier <paths...> --check
prettier <paths...> --write
rules: --check reports formatting differences; --write changes files.
Quote globs so Prettier expands them consistently. Respect project configuration and ignore files.
Reference: https://prettier.io/docs/cli

summary: Run Vitest once or interactively from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.
syntax:
vitest [test-filter]
vitest run [test-filter] [--coverage]
vitest --watch
rules: run performs one pass for CI; default development behavior watches. Filters match file paths.
Coverage needs the matching @vitest/coverage-v8 or Istanbul provider version installed; stop watch mode with Ctrl-C.

summary: Develop and build with Vite from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.

vite [root] [--host <host>] [--port <port>]
vite build [--mode <mode>]
vite preview [--host <host>]
rules: Dev server runs until Ctrl-C; build writes production assets. Vite transpiles TypeScript without type checking.
preview serves the built output for local inspection, not production hosting. Bind to loopback for local use.

summary: Inspect a package before publication from a Bash/Zsh developer terminal.
syntax:
npm pack --dry-run
npm pack
pnpm pack
rules: Inspect the package file list before publishing; check for secrets and unnecessary files.
pack creates a local tarball, not a registry release. Lifecycle scripts may run; --dry-run previews npm contents.

title: Watch TypeScript checks
summary: Continuously check a configured project after edits.
syntax: tsc --project <config> --watch [--noEmit]
rules: Watch mode runs until Ctrl-C. --noEmit avoids generated JavaScript.
Use --build --watch for referenced-project builds instead.
Reference: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/compiler-options.html

title: Functions and local variables
summary: Functions run in the calling shell; return leaves the function, exit terminates its shell.
syntax:
name() { local value="$1"; commands; return status; }
name "$argument"
rules: Functions run in the calling shell; return leaves the function, exit terminates its shell.
local is Bash/Zsh, not POSIX; use a subshell function for POSIX isolation. Dynamic scope means callees can see locals.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Positional arguments and getopts
summary: getopts parses short options and stops at the first operand; -- ends option parsing.
syntax:
while getopts ":n:v" opt; do case "$opt" in ... esac; done
shift "$((OPTIND - 1))"
for arg in "$@"; do ...; done
rules: getopts parses short options and stops at the first operand; -- ends option parsing.
A leading colon lets scripts distinguish missing option arguments from unknown options. Reset OPTIND=1 for a new parse.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Arrays and explicit dialects
summary: Quoted array expansion preserves each element as an argument, including empty elements.
rules: Quoted array expansion preserves each element as an argument, including empty elements.
Bash indexes from zero, native Zsh from one; arrays are not POSIX. Do not assume scalar word splitting or glob behavior matches across shells.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Safe glob and NUL filename workflows
summary: Newlines are valid in filenames; NUL is the safe record separator. Prefix paths with ./ and quote expansions.
syntax:
shopt -s nullglob
for file in ./*.txt; do ...; done
find ./input -type f -print0 | xargs -0 -r command
rules: Newlines are valid in filenames; NUL is the safe record separator. Prefix paths with ./ and quote expansions.
Bash nullglob differs from Zsh NOMATCH; GNU xargs -r skips empty input. Never parse ls output.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

references.title: Safe glob and NUL filename workflows

title: Read records with explicit IFS
summary: IFS= and read -r preserve leading spaces and backslashes; handle an unterminated final line explicitly.
syntax:
while IFS= read -r line || [ -n "$line" ]; do ...; done < file
IFS=: read -r name value
rules: IFS= and read -r preserve leading spaces and backslashes; handle an unterminated final line explicitly.
Read loops fed by pipelines may run in a subshell; redirect a file to retain loop variables. Delimiter splitting is not a general CSV parser.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Exit status and recoverable checks
summary: Capture $? immediately; ! negates it, so capture inside an ordinary else branch.
syntax:
if command; then ...; else rc=$?; ...; fi
command; rc=$?
return "$rc"
rules: Capture $? immediately; ! negates it, so capture inside an ordinary else branch.
Nonzero can mean a valid negative result (grep 1), not always a system failure (grep 2). set -e is context-dependent and does not replace explicit checks.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Pipeline failure propagation
summary: Without pipefail a pipeline reports only its final command; with it the rightmost failing command determines status.
syntax:
set -o pipefail
producer | consumer
# Bash only: codes=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}")
rules: Without pipefail a pipeline reports only its final command; with it the rightmost failing command determines status.
Capture Bash PIPESTATUS before any other command; Zsh uses pipestatus with one-based indexing. Early consumers can cause SIGPIPE; avoid head when producer success matters.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Temporary resources and traps
summary: Create a unique private directory; quote its path and register cleanup immediately.
syntax:
scratch=$(mktemp -d) || exit
trap 'rm -rf -- "$scratch"' EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT
trap 'exit 143' TERM
rules: Create a unique private directory; quote its path and register cleanup immediately.
EXIT cleanup also runs on handled failure; SIGKILL cannot be trapped. Keep signal handlers explicit and avoid assuming errexit catches every failure.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Subshell state and failure
summary: Parenthesized groups isolate cwd and variables but retain file side effects.
syntax:
( cd directory && command )
if ( command ); then ...; else rc=$?; ...; fi
rules: Parenthesized groups isolate cwd and variables but retain file side effects.
A subshell reports its last command status; explicitly short-circuit steps to avoid a later success hiding a failed cd.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Process substitution with checked producers
summary: Bash/Zsh process substitution supplies a path instead of a pipeline, so loop state can remain in the caller.
rules: Bash/Zsh process substitution supplies a path instead of a pipeline, so loop state can remain in the caller.
Producer status is not automatically the consumer status. The Bash tasks capture $! immediately and wait explicitly; use temporary files if multiple producers need dependable status handling.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Here-documents and file descriptors
summary: Quoting the delimiter suppresses substitutions; an unquoted delimiter permits expansion. The terminator must occupy its own line.
syntax:
cat <<'END'
literal $text
END
command >out.txt 2>err.txt
command 2>&1 >out.txt
rules: Quoting the delimiter suppresses substitutions; an unquoted delimiter permits expansion. The terminator must occupy its own line.
Descriptor redirections apply left to right. Separate stderr to keep data streams parseable; <<- strips tabs, not spaces.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Command substitution and multiline values
summary: Command substitution strips all trailing newlines; quoted expansion retains internal whitespace. NUL bytes cannot be stored in shell variables.
syntax:
if value=$(command); then printf "%s\n" "$value"; else ...; fi
value=$(command; printf .); value=${value%.}
rules: Command substitution strips all trailing newlines; quoted expansion retains internal whitespace. NUL bytes cannot be stored in shell variables.
Check the assignment status. A sentinel preserves trailing newlines only when producer status is propagated explicitly.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Sed and cut transformations
summary: sed edits streams by default; avoid incompatible in-place -i forms across GNU/BSD.
syntax:
sed -n 's/^key=//p' file
cut -d: -f1 file
rules: sed edits streams by default; avoid incompatible in-place -i forms across GNU/BSD.
cut splits literal delimiters, not quoted CSV. Check source status and write a separate result before replacing inputs.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Awk validation and aggregation
summary: awk associative iteration order is unspecified; sort output explicitly with LC_ALL=C for repeatability.
syntax: awk -F, '... {sum[$1]+=$2} END {for (key in sum) print key,sum[key]}' file
rules: awk associative iteration order is unspecified; sort output explicitly with LC_ALL=C for repeatability.
Specify input format and validate fields before arithmetic; this simple delimiter format does not support quoted CSV or decimal locale conventions.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Sort, uniq and deterministic streams
summary: uniq combines adjacent equal lines, so sort first for global counts.
syntax:
LC_ALL=C sort file | uniq -c
LC_ALL=C sort -t: -k2,2n -k1,1
rules: uniq combines adjacent equal lines, so sort first for global counts.
Set locale explicitly. Numeric ordering differs from lexical ordering; use secondary keys for stable ties. These tasks use newline records, not arbitrary filenames.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Jq schema checks and recovery
summary: Quote jq programs and pass data through --arg/--argjson, never interpolate it into program source.
syntax:
jq -e '... or error("invalid")' file
jq --arg name "$value" '{name:$name}'
rules: Quote jq programs and pass data through --arg/--argjson, never interpolate it into program source.
-e reports false/null as nonzero; malformed input and error() are failures. Check schema and separate successful results from diagnostics.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Git diff, stage and restore
summary: The index is the next commit snapshot; worktree edits after add remain unstaged.
syntax:
git diff -- path
git add -- path
git diff --cached -- path
git restore --staged -- path
rules: The index is the next commit snapshot; worktree edits after add remain unstaged.
restore --staged resets the index from HEAD without discarding worktree edits. restore without --staged overwrites working files; inspect and back up first. Requires Git 2.23+.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Stash apply and recovery
summary: Stash saves tracked changes; -u also includes untracked files, not ignored files.
syntax:
git stash push -u -m "label"
git stash list
git stash apply stash@{0}
# drop only after inspection
rules: Stash saves tracked changes; -u also includes untracked files, not ignored files.
apply retains the stash even when successful, and conflicts require manual resolution. Avoid pop while learning so recovery data remains available.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Conflict stages and abort
summary: Unmerged index stages hold base, ours and theirs for ordinary content conflicts; add/delete conflicts can omit stages.
syntax:
git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U
git ls-files -u
git show :1:path
git show :2:path
git show :3:path
git merge --abort
rules: Unmerged index stages hold base, ours and theirs for ordinary content conflicts; add/delete conflicts can omit stages.
Inspect stages before editing. merge --abort is for an active merge and can fail to reconstruct pre-merge uncommitted changes; start with a clean disposable repository.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.

title: Inspect and abort a rebase
summary: Rebase replays commits; during a conflict ours is the upstream/rebased side and theirs is the commit being replayed.
syntax:
git status --short
git rebase --show-current-patch
git rebase --abort
rules: Rebase replays commits; during a conflict ours is the upstream/rebased side and theirs is the commit being replayed.
Inspect current patch and stages before resolving; --abort restores the original branch. Do not rewrite shared history; these examples never push.
Validated on Bash 5.2.21; dialect restrictions are stated on each practical card.
